issues.legal_issue: The registering authority lacks discretion to reassess the price of a public auction monitored and confirmed by a court under the undervaluation provisions.
material_facts: In both matters, property was sold through a court-supervised process conducted by a receiver or official liquidator after invitations for offers were published.
The sales involved bidding, and the courts confirmed the accepted bids after supervising the sale process.
The registering authority later assessed the properties at higher values and demanded additional stamp duty and registration fees.
issues.conclusion: Section 47A did not give the registering authority discretion to reassess the price in a public auction monitored by the court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47A of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as amended in West Bengal, read with Rule 3 of the West Bengal Stamp (Prevention of Undervaluation of Instruments) Rules, 2001, addresses undervaluation and permits action where the registering officer has reason to believe the stated value is not true. A court-monitored public auction conducted through the court’s process does not, merely because the registering authority would place a higher value on the property, provide such a basis. The Court relied on the purpose of the undervaluation provisions discussed in Govt. of Andhra Pradesh v. P. Laxmi Devi and V.N. Devadoss v. Chief Revenue Control Office-cum-Inspector, and held that V.N. Devadoss was not per incuriam. It recognized that Kayjay Industries v. Asnew Drums described court sales as forced sales, but held that their competitive element and court supervision remain relevant. The Court did not endorse the lower court’s interpretation of the market-value formula, its proposed route for the registering authority to approach the court, or its stated conditions for treating a court sale as an open-market sale.

predicates.court_monitored_public_auction: The property was offered for sale through a public auction conducted under a court’s supervision.
predicates.sale_confirmed_by_court: The court reviewed the sale and confirmed the accepted bid.

issues.definition: When a public auction is supervised by a court and the court confirms the sale, the registering authority cannot reassess the auction price.

issues.legal_issue: The market value of property sold through a court-monitored auction reflects the price an actual bidder is willing to pay in the circumstances of the sale, rather than a notional value detached from those circumstances.
material_facts: One property was occupied by numerous tenants and daytime vendors, which affected the value a purchaser could obtain from it.
For the other property, an earlier offering did not attract bids at the reserve price, a second auction was held, and the accepted bid was obtained through a court-monitored process.
The courts accepted the bids after overseeing the respective sale processes.
issues.conclusion: The relevant value is the price obtainable from the accepted bidder in the facts and prevailing circumstances, not a notional price.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(16B) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, defines market value by reference to the price a property would fetch if sold in the open market, and Section 47A and Rule 3 provide for addressing undervaluation. In applying those provisions to court-monitored auctions, the Court stated that the market value is the price the highest bidder is willing to pay in the facts and prevailing circumstances. It relied on the purpose of the undervaluation provisions described in Govt. of Andhra Pradesh v. P. Laxmi Devi and V.N. Devadoss v. Chief Revenue Control Office-cum-Inspector, and considered the competitive element of court auctions discussed in Kayjay Industries v. Asnew Drums. Property circumstances such as tenancy, and the results of repeated auction efforts, may affect the price obtainable.

predicates.court_monitored_auction: The property was offered for sale through an auction supervised by a court.
predicates.accepted_bid_after_competitive_process: A bid emerged from a competitive sale process and was accepted after the court reviewed the process.

issues.definition: When a court supervises a competitive auction and accepts a bid, that bid reflects market value in the circumstances of the sale.
